problems_fixed.what: Audit 'degenerate': old problem 10 - 3 + 2 used only equal-priority add/subtract, so it did not test the lesson's core different-priority idea. Replaced with a problem mixing multiply against add and subtract, and rebuilt both misconceptions to real determinate errors.
Audit 'bad_misconception_message': ignore_bracket had check 'equals_17'; ignoring the bracket in 5+3x4-10 gives 7, not 17. Set expect to 7.
Audit 'bad_misconception_message': square_wrong had check 'equals_10'; expanding (2+3)^2 as 2^2+3^2=13 gives final 13-8=5, not 10. Set expect to 5.

Audit two issues on 2^4-(3x2+1)^0x10. Removed the vacuous 'bracket_error' misconception (any non-zero base to power 0 is 1, so it can never change the answer). Rewrote the mislabelled 'index_error' (its message described the correct working) into 'subtract_before_multiply' (expect 150), and added a genuine 'power_as_base' misconception (treating 7^0 as 7 gives 16-70 = -54).
problems_fixed.old: misconceptions: zero_power(16), bracket_error(null/vacuous), index_error(150 with a message describing correct working)
problems_fixed.new: misconceptions: zero_power(16), power_as_base(-54), subtract_before_multiply(150 with corrected message)

opener_concept: A lunch bill: 1 sandwich (£3) + 2 juices at £2 each. Students naturally total the juices (2 x £2 = £4) before adding the sandwich, doing multiplication before addition by common sense; the reveal names this as BIDMAS. A second box (change from £20 after 3 sandwiches at £3) reinforces multiply-before-subtract.
